headline: High: Mentat’s filesystem writes and broad egress can turn shared-file workflows into leakage and cascading errors; the course repo itself is non-runnable, limiting prompt-injection risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a non-runnable course repo with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest B’s outputs. Profile B reads and writes files and uses stdin/stdout, so if a user manually bridges A’s content into B, prompt injection is possible, but the pathway is not default and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF the user copies A-generated text into B’s prompt or files
IF B is configured to treat file contents as instructions
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate folders
Review copied text before pasting into B
Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from inputs
Disable any workflow that auto-loads repo text into B

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no network egress, while B reads selected files, writes files, and sends context to a configured model provider. If sensitive files are placed in the shared workspace, B can transmit them off-box; A does not add leakage, but the pair still creates a default file-to-API exposure path through B.
conditions: IF sensitive files are opened in the same workspace that B reads
IF B’s provider configuration remains enabled
mitigations: Do not place secrets in the shared workspace
Run B only on redacted copies
Verify provider logging/retention settings before use
Use a separate non-sensitive project directory
Rotate any secrets that were already present in files B may read

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network capabilities, but B can write the filesystem and modify git state, with shared state explicitly via filesystem. That creates a real conflict surface if both are pointed at the same directory or repo, even though A itself is not an active writer.
conditions: IF A and B are run against the same working tree
IF B performs edits while another instance or process also edits the same files
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout
Pause other editors before running B
Commit or stash changes before invoking B
Use git worktrees for parallel work
Review diffs before applying them

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a course repo and B is a coding assistant that proposes diffs after user confirmation. If A’s materials are fed into B as authoritative guidance, B may propagate mistakes into edits or commits. The confirmation step reduces but does not eliminate the cascade, so medium fits better than low.
conditions: IF A’s text is used as the source of truth for B’s edits
IF the user approves B’s proposed diffs without independent review
mitigations: Require a second human review of B’s diffs
Cross-check A-derived claims against primary sources
Limit B to small, isolated edits
Ask B to cite the exact file lines it used
Reject diffs that change more than one concern at a time

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is documented for A, and B only explicitly handles source code plus model-provider API keys. The pair therefore shows only a generic compliance gap: B’s external model-provider calls may be incompatible with some local-only workflows, but the profiles do not evidence a specific regulated-data violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into files B reads
IF the configured model provider’s retention terms conflict with the operator’s policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B’s inputs
Review provider terms before use
Use a local model if policy requires it
Document the data flow for the workspace
Delete temporary files after the session
